rj_ragout_taverne.intro: Slow carbs, fibre and protein: lasting energy against the cold of the night.
etapes: The opening: open the tin of beans completely.
The cutting: slice the smoked sausage into thick rounds, add it to the beans and stir.
The heating: put the mess tin (or the open tin) on a flat stone at the edge of the embers, and let it simmer until it bubbles gently.
The melting: take it off the fire with gloves or improvised tongs, and throw the cheese cubes in.
Serving: let it melt for 1 minute. With a spoon, when the cheese turns stringy.
attention: Never heat a closed tin: it explodes. An open tin can be heated at the edge of the embers, but its inner coating doesn't like a fierce fire: it's best to pour the contents into the mess tin.
Never use a stone taken from water or very damp: the water trapped inside can make it burst in the fire.

recette.cuisson: On a hot stone, in the tin or mess tin
ingredients: 1 tin of beans in tomato sauce (baked beans)
50 g of hard cheese (Comté, Beaufort) in cubes

rj_grilled_cheese.intro: Very high in calories: fat to restart the body's boiler in cold weather.
etapes: The sandwich: put the cheese and bacon between the two slices of bread.
The wrapping: wrap the sandwich firmly in foil.
The press: heat a flat, clean, dry stone at the edge of the fire. It must be very hot.
The cooking: put the sandwich on a nice flat bed of embers, then the hot stone on top, like a panini press.
The result: 3 to 5 minutes each side. The bread should be crispy and the cheese completely melted.
attention: Never use a stone taken from water or very damp: the water trapped inside can make it burst in the fire.
Handle the stone with two sticks or thick gloves.

ingredients: 3 thick slices of melting cheese (raclette, cheddar or reblochon)
2 slices of bacon or cured ham

etapes: The searing: in the mess tin, sauté the mushrooms in the oil over small flames until golden.
The broth: crumble the stock cube over them and pour in a big glass of water (250 ml).
The reduction: let it boil for 5 minutes over the embers.
The binding: off the heat, add the cheese and stir hard until you get a creamy sauce.
The trick: pour it over a potato baked in the embers, or eat it as a thick soup with bread.
attention: Shop-bought mushrooms only. Never cook a wild mushroom unless you're absolutely sure: some are deadly.

recette.cuisson: In the mess tin (hung or on a tripod)
ingredients: 1 handful of shop-bought mushrooms (fresh, or dried and rehydrated)
2 portions of spreadable cheese (like Laughing Cow)

rj_pain_elmoth.intro: Compact carbs: keeps in the pack and gets eaten on the move the next day.
etapes: The kneading: in the mess tin or the flour bag, add the salt, sugar, and the water little by little. Mix by hand until you get a firm dough that no longer sticks.
The shape: divide the dough and flatten it into thin flatbreads, 1 cm at most so they cook through.
The natural oven: brush the ash off a flat stone heated at the edge of the fire. It must be scorching.
The cooking: put the flatbreads straight onto the stone, without fat.
The timing: 5 to 8 minutes each side. The flatbread should sound hollow. Eat it hot, or wrap it in a cloth for the road.
attention: Never use a stone taken from water or very damp: the water trapped inside can make it burst in the fire.

recette.jeu: The Lord of the Rings and fantasy
ingredients: 100 g of wheat flour (weighed at home in a sealed bag)

rj_cafe_cowboy.intro: Caffeine against tiredness, sugar and magnesium from the chocolate.
etapes: The boil: bring the water to a full boil in the mess tin.
The brewing: take it off the heat, throw the ground coffee into the water and stir once.
The settling: let it stand 3 to 4 minutes without touching it, out of the wind. The grounds sink and settle at the bottom.
The secret: put the square of chocolate at the bottom of your mug.
Serving: pour very gently, without shaking the mess tin, to leave the grounds at the bottom. Stir to melt the chocolate.
attention: A drop of cold water poured onto the coffee helps the grounds sink. Don't drink the bottom.

ingredients: 1 square of dark chocolate (or a little sugar)

rj_onigiri.intro: Slow carbs: a full stamina gauge before a long walk.
etapes: The gentle fire: rice and water in the mess tin, lid closed with a stone on top. Bring to the boil over the embers, then move the tin back and leave for 15 minutes on very low heat, never opening it.
The rest: off the heat, let it steam for 10 minutes, still covered.
The shaping: let it cool slightly, wet your hands with salted water. Take a handful of rice, make a hollow and slip in a spoonful of flaked tuna.
The triangle: press hard between your hands to form a compact triangle. Wrap the base in seaweed to hold it without sticky fingers.
attention: Cooked rice and opened tuna don't keep: eat the onigiri the same day, and not after a hot day in the pack.

ingredients: 100 g of short-grain rice (sushi rice), washed at home
1 small tin of tuna in water (or chopped cooked bacon)

rj_soupe_monstre.intro: Rehydration, collagen and minerals: the best defence bonus against frost.
etapes: The searing: brown the meat at the bottom of the hot mess tin, with a little fat.
The deluge: just cover with water, and add the onion, carrot and crumbled stock cube.
The long cook: put the mess tin on a tripod or two stable stones, over medium embers. Let it simmer 1 h to 1 h 30 while you put up the shelter. The gentler and longer, the more tender the meat.
Tasting: serve piping hot in the mug. Add water if it reduces too much.
attention: Shop-bought onion: wild garlic and “wild onions” have deadly look-alikes (lily of the valley, autumn crocus). See the species sheets.
Poultry and pork must be cooked through: cut the biggest piece, the flesh must no longer be pink and the juices must run clear.

ingredients: 200 g of braising meat (beef, shop-bought game or pork shank)

rj_galette_stalker.intro: Compact energy, bottom-of-the-pack ingredients that keep a long time.
etapes: The mix: in the mess tin, mix the flakes and flour, then add the lukewarm water little by little until you get a thick dough, like modelling clay. Salt and pepper.
The flatbreads: form balls, then flatten them into thick flatbreads the size of your palm.
The fire test: heat the oil in the pan or the mess-tin lid, on the embers.
The frying: 3 to 4 minutes each side, until you get a golden, crispy crust.
Serving: hot, ideally with a piece of corned beef, for a real tunnel survivor's meal.
attention: Hot oil over the fire: keep the pan very stable, and never any water in it.

recette.cuisson: In a bivouac pan or the mess-tin lid

rj_porridge.intro: Low glycaemic index: steady energy for hours of walking in the cold.
etapes: The soaking: in the cold mess tin, mix the oats, dried fruit and water.
The bubbling: over medium embers, gently bring to the boil, stirring constantly so the bottom doesn't stick.
The thickening: as soon as it boils and thickens (3 to 5 minutes), take it off the heat.
The finish: add the honey, cover for 2 minutes so the dried fruit plumps up. It warms you right from waking up.

ingredients: 200 ml of water (or melted snow, boiled)
1 handful of dried fruit (raisins, cranberries, almonds)
1 teaspoon of honey or brown sugar

rj_lembas.intro: Dense carbs: the trappers' bread par excellence.
etapes: The ration dough: in a freezer bag or the mess tin, mix flour, powdered milk and salt. Add a splash of water and knead until you get a soft, elastic ball.
The support: cut a green-wood branch (hazel or birch) the size of a broom handle, and strip the bark off the last 20 centimetres.
The winding: stretch the dough into a long, thin rope and wind it in a spiral around the stripped part, pressing the ends down firmly.
The cooking: above the embers, not in the flames, turning regularly.
The result: in 10 to 15 minutes, the bread puffs up, browns and comes away by itself. Fill the hole with a square of chocolate or cheese.
attention: No yew, cherry laurel or unknown wood: they're poisonous. Hazel, birch or willow.

recette.jeu: The Lord of the Rings and Green Hell
ingredients: 100 g of flour with a pinch of baking powder

rj_ragout_goule.intro: Salt against cramps, protein that keeps a long time.
etapes: The base: soften the diced onion in a little fat at the bottom of the mess tin, until translucent.
The meat: add the block of corned beef and mash it with the spoon.
The bubbling: pour in the water and let it simmer 5 minutes over the embers.
The thickener: crumble 3 or 4 crackers into it. They soak up the juice and give a thick, rustic mash.
Eating: piping hot. +50% energy gauge.

rj_jerky.intro: Pure protein, almost fat-free: a snack that keeps in the pack.
etapes: The salting: salt and spice the strips on all sides, and let them rest 30 minutes on a clean surface.
The safety sear: dip the strips in boiling water for 1 minute, or sear them quickly on the grill. The meat must be heated through before drying.
The drying rack: build a small green-wood tripod, or stretch cords 60 cm above dying embers.
The hanging: thread the strips onto green-wood skewers and hang them in the heat.
The smoking: no flames, just gentle heat and hardwood smoke (oak, beech), for 3 to 4 hours.
The result: the meat turns dark and dry, but stays supple. Store it in a clean, closed bag.
attention: Campfire drying isn't industrial preserving: eat this jerky within 2 to 3 days, and throw it away if it smells bad or turns damp.
Shop-bought beef only: wild game can carry parasites that drying doesn't kill.

recette.jeu: The Long Dark and ARK: Survival Evolved
recette.cuisson: Drying and smoking over the embers
ingredients: 200 g of lean beef (topside) in 5 mm strips

rj_crispy_boite.intro: Fast sugars and potassium: morale and mental energy pick up at once.
etapes: The venting: open the tin and pour off half the syrup (drink it, it's an energy shot).
The crumble: crumble the biscuits over the fruit, add the cinnamon.
The fire: put the open tin (or the mess tin) firmly on a nest of small embers.
The caramelising: let it bubble gently for 10 minutes. The syrup reduces and the biscuit forms a crust.
Serving: take it off with a tool or thick cloth, and let it cool for 2 minutes before eating with a spoon.
attention: Never heat a closed tin: it explodes. An open tin can be heated at the edge of the embers, but its inner coating doesn't like a fierce fire: it's best to pour the contents into the mess tin.

recette.cuisson: In the tin or mess tin, on the embers
ingredients: 1 tin of fruit in syrup (pineapple, peaches or apricots)

rj_elixir_mana.intro: Vitamin C and warmth: real comfort when it's cold.
etapes: The harvest: rinse the needles and chop them roughly with the knife to release the aromas.
The heating: bring the water to a full boil.
The steeping: take it off the heat, add the needles and ginger, and cover.
The rest: 10 to 12 minutes out of the wind. The liquid turns golden.
The strain: pour into the mug, holding back the needles, then add the honey.
attention: Yew is deadly and looks like a fir: flat, soft needles, dark green on top, no citrus smell, and red berries. See its species sheet. Also avoid thuja and ornamental conifers.
Not advised for pregnant women: some pine needles are not recommended during pregnancy.

ingredients: 1 handful of young pine or fir needles, identified with certainty
1 piece of ginger (brought along), or young bramble shoots

rj_fondue_pelerin.intro: Fat and protein galore: the perfect dish for a night below zero.
etapes: The aroma: rub the bottom and sides of the mess tin with the halved garlic clove, and leave it at the bottom.
The start: pour in the wine (or apple juice) and bring to a simmer over gentle embers.
The cascade: add the cheese in three goes, stirring constantly in figures of eight.
The smoothness: keep the heat very gentle. The cheese must melt without burning or splitting. Move the tin back if it gets too hot.
The action: spear the bread on the end of a wooden skewer and dip it in the tin, in the middle of the group.
attention: Cooked wine keeps a little alcohol: use the apple juice version for children.

ingredients: 150 g of pressed cheese (Comté, Abondance or Emmental) grated or in cubes
50 ml of dry white wine (in a small flask), or tart apple juice

rj_fondue_pelerin.source: Original Bivaska recipe, inspired by Steep and Horizon. Unofficial: Bivaska is not affiliated with or endorsed by any publisher of the games mentioned

rj_galettes_ration.intro: Oats: slow energy, iron and fibre. Ultra-light to carry.
etapes: The shelter mix: in the mess tin, mix the oats, powdered milk, salt and raisins.
The hydration: add the water spoon by spoon until you get a very compact, sticky dough.
The compacting: shape small, very flat, dense cakes the size of a bank card.
The heating: put them on a scorching flat stone, brushed and dry, or on the upturned mess-tin lid set on the embers.
The result: 6 to 8 minutes each side, until they're dry and rigid. Well dried, they keep about a week in a sealed bag.
attention: Never use a stone taken from water or very damp: the water trapped inside can make it burst in the fire.

recette.cuisson: On a stone or mess-tin lid (dry cooking)
ingredients: 80 g of oat flour (or flakes crushed with the knife)
